title: Checkpoint: Making Decisions
intro: Check how well you can compare values, combine conditions, and choose between branches with if and match.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
command = "halt"
match command:
    case "go" | "start":
        print("Moving")
    case "stop" | "halt":
        print("Stopping")
    case _:
        print("Unknown command")
questions.explanation: | lets one case match several values. "halt" matches the second case.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
color = "green"
match color:
    case "red":
        print("Stop")
    case other:
        print("Unknown:", other)
questions.explanation: A bare name in a case pattern is a capture pattern: it matches any value and binds it, so the last case always runs when nothing before it matched. That is why it must come last.

questions.question: What is wrong with this code?
options: It uses = instead of ==, so Python raises SyntaxError

questions.explanation: A single = assigns a value; comparing needs ==. Python stops with a SyntaxError and even suggests the fix.
